failure_mode: PROFINET on side A is run as IRT (RT class 3) or on switches that are not PROFINET-conformant, so the VLAN/QoS scheme in the draft cannot protect the cycle; logger frames on the shared trunk cause PROFINET cycle overrun or device drop-out
effect: Side A winch/base-station PROFINET devices lose connection or report cycle faults; hoist control on side A degraded or stopped
cause: PROFINET RT class and switch conformance class not established before sharing was accepted; QoS assumed sufficient

failure_mode: Shared fibre becomes a common-mode single point of failure: one fibre break or switch failure now removes both PROFINET and SWS logger data for side A simultaneously
effect: Loss of hoist control communication and loss of SWS monitoring/logging evidence at the same time; no independent record of the event
cause: Logger path and control path routed over the same physical medium and same base-station switches

failure_mode: Base-station switch configuration drift: a later maintenance change (VLAN, trunk, port role, firmware) silently removes the segregation or rate limit on an SWS port
effect: DEMO-NET-001/002 mitigations no longer in force without anyone noticing; broadcast storm or SWS frames on PLC VLAN become possible again
cause: No configuration baseline, change control, or periodic verification of switch config defined for the logger ports

failure_mode: PROFINET ring redundancy (e.g. MRP) on the fibre backbone interacts with the logger VLAN: logger VLAN spans the ring, or a logger port is bridged back into the ring, creating a loop or interfering with ring reconfiguration
effect: Ring reconfiguration slower than PROFINET watchdog, or a broadcast loop across both VLANs; side A devices drop out
cause: Logger VLAN topology not designed against the existing ring topology; ring protocol membership of logger ports undefined

failure_mode: SWS logger port on a base station used as an uncontrolled entry point to the control backbone (laptop, rogue device, or wrong cable plugged into the logger port)
effect: Unauthorised traffic or device on the backbone; possible disturbance of PROFINET or access to PLC network
cause: Logger port is a live Ethernet port in the field with no port security / MAC limiting / physical lock defined

failure_mode: SWS logger frames dropped by QoS or ingress rate limit under load, with no end-to-end acknowledgement, so the logger record has silent gaps
effect: Incomplete SWS log used later as evidence or for maintenance decisions without the gap being known
cause: Logger data is lowest priority on the trunk and rate limited per the mitigation, but no sequence/heartbeat check at the logger is specified

failure_mode: Physical-separation option consumes the spare fibre cores on side A, leaving no spare for repair of a damaged PROFINET core
effect: A future single-core fault on the PROFINET path cannot be repaired by re-splicing to a spare; longer outage
cause: Spare-core policy not checked before allocating cores to the logger
